consumer_seed: The Ofcom Connected Nations Spring 2026 update was published on 13 May 2026.
The update reports a snapshot of UK mobile coverage and fixed broadband availability as of January 2026.
The fixed-broadband update covers availability from fixed-line and fixed-wireless-access networks.
The report defines decent broadband as at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
Mobile coverage is reported using signal-strength predictions supplied by the four mobile network operators.
Full fibre was reported available to 24.9 million UK residential premises, equal to 82% of 30.5 million homes.
Ofcom reported 1.2 million additional homes gaining access to full fibre in the six months to January 2026.
Full-fibre take-up across residential and commercial premises reached 12.4 million, or 47% of premises with access.
Gigabit-capable broadband availability reached 89%, or 27.1 million homes.
Ofcom estimated that 4,000 premises lacked access to affordable decent broadband.
Predicted good 4G geographic coverage from all mobile network operators reached 84% of UK landmass.
Overall 5G coverage outside premises from all mobile network operators increased from 47% to 64%.
The Ofcom Map Your Mobile news release was published on 29 May 2026.
Ofcom reported that one million people had used Map Your Mobile.
The checker accepts a postcode and displays a map of networks available in that area.
The checker supplies a score indicating which company performs best in the user's postal district.
The checker combines crowdsourced Opensignal data with predictive information from UK mobile networks.
Ofcom says the checker is regularly updated with fresh data and accepts user feedback.
Map Your Mobile can indicate whether coverage is likely to work inside a house.
Ofcom presents the checker as a research tool to use before signing up to a new mobile deal.
A postcode search returns two information sets: coverage and performance.
Coverage results show likely 4G or 5G availability indoors and outdoors and classify signal as good or variable.
Performance results estimate the likelihood of successfully streaming video in the local postal district.
Trees, buildings and wall thickness can cause actual experience to differ from the coverage prediction.
Ofcom suggests Wi-Fi calling when indoor mobile calls are difficult and a broadband connection is available.
The checker includes the four main UK mobile network operators.
Other UK mobile operators provide service over one of the four main networks.
Postal-district results are not representative of national mobile coverage.
Performance scores are guidance because local variations can occur.
Local reception can be affected by mast power and distance, terrain, buildings, congestion, construction materials, weather and handset antenna quality.
The Ofcom emergency-calls compliance programme was published on 31 October 2025.
The programme was last updated and closed on 8 June 2026.
The programme assessed regulated providers' compliance with obligations concerning emergency calls.
General Conditions require providers to take all necessary measures to ensure uninterrupted access to emergency organisations for offered voice services.
Providers must make accurate and reliable caller-location information available for 999 and 112 calls where technically feasible.
The programme identified General Conditions A3.2(b), A3.5 and A3.6 as the relevant legal provisions.
Ofcom reported no specific issues warranting further formal enforcement action at closure.
Ofcom identified measures providers should take to support compliance and set them out in a letter to industry.
Ofcom expects providers to implement the identified measures where appropriate and proportionate.
Ofcom said it would continue monitoring compliance and remained prepared to take firm enforcement action for serious concerns.
